sources.author: existing-product
sources.annotation: The site's own precedent: a grid of face-out covers that morph into a modal reader via motion layoutId. This is the pattern Things I Love must not simply repeat.
take: layoutId shared-element morph is already proven in this codebase
labelled stone fallback for missing artwork
soft contact shadow to make a flat image read as a physical object
muted per-item accent used only for small marks, never fills
avoid: cover-to-modal as the literal interaction, which would make two pages feel like one template
the 2:3 uniform aspect ratio, which products do not share
shelf plinth metaphor, which belongs to books

sources.author: agent
sources.annotation: Verified. The dominant /uses pattern: category headings, then item name plus one line of personal reason. The reason carries the value, not the list.
take: one specific first-person line per item, with a date or a switch story
avoid: affiliate links and their disclosure burden - user chose no links
software and desk-app categories, which are out of scope
long undifferentiated bullet lists, which do not suit 5 items

sources.author: agent
sources.annotation: Verified. Kevin Kelly's rule since 2000: 'We only post things we like and ignore the rest.' Positive-only, short entry, category tag, reviewer byline.
take: the positive-only rule, adopted as an explicit exclusion in the contract
short entry length as a discipline
avoid: category tags and archive structure, which solve a thousand-item problem
multiple reviewers - this page is one voice

sources.author: agent
sources.annotation: Verified. About 1,200 titles with a two-colour highlight system: green for excellent, light blue for above average.
take: the idea that a quality mark lets a long list still show a short favourite set
avoid: the mark itself - at 4-5 items every item is a favourite, so a rank carries zero information and adds noise

sources.author: agent
sources.annotation: Verified. Consumer product recommendation site: product image first, monthly top 5, shop links throughout.
take: product image as the primary identifier
a small fixed count reads as curation
avoid: storefront mechanics, shop links, and influencer framing, which conflict with the no-links decision

sources.author: agent
sources.annotation: Directory of 928+ personal /uses pages. Establishes the genre and its convention, and shows how saturated the dev-tools version is.
avoid: the /uses framing itself - physical products only keeps this page distinct

tensions.tension: The site's own bookshelf is the closest and strongest reference, and also the thing this page must not duplicate. Reusing its interaction is the fastest path and the worst outcome.
tensions.resolution: Reuse the motion primitives and the fallback pattern. Vary the reveal model. That is open decision D1.

tensions.tension: Every consumer-product reference in the genre earns its density from volume and links. This page has 5 items and no links.
tensions.resolution: Do not scale a catalog down. Design for 5 directly: low density, large objects, the reason treated as primary content rather than as a caption.
